St George's is entering an exciting new chapter.

Academically ambitious

pageCache.pageTitle: St George’s Ascot partners with St George’s School Windsor Castle to create a new through school | St Georges Ascot
pageCache.text:
St George’s Ascot partners with St George’s School Windsor Castle to create a new through school
Today it was announced that we are creating a new through school by joining with St George’s School Windsor Castle and supported by St Albans Education Group (STAEG). St George’s School Windsor Castle is an award-winning day and boarding prep school and home to the choristers of St George’s Chapel. The new co-educational school - St George’s School, Windsor and Ascot - will offer a seamless educational journey from ages 3 to 18 with access to excellent facilities across the schools’ existing two sites.
Beyond our shared name, we have a great deal in common with St George’s School Windsor Castle. We both have long and proud histories, strong academic and co-curricular traditions, particularly in music and the creative arts, and offer a range of boarding options that reflect the needs of modern families. Just as importantly, our ethos, values and vision align and there is a real sense of shared purpose between the two schools.
As part of creating a through school, we will begin to welcome boys to Years 7 and 9 at St George’s Ascot from September 2027. Moving gradually to a co-educational model will enrich the experience of every pupil while preserving the traditions of excellence that have been the cornerstone of our success. By welcoming both girls and boys, we will broaden perspectives in the classroom and create even more opportunities for collaboration, leadership, and personal development.
This represents an important step, one within the school's long tradition of evolution. Since its foundation in 1877, St George's has adapted over time while remaining true to its core purpose – broadening access while strengthening what we offer.
We are excited about working with Emma Károlyi, Head at St George’s School Windsor Castle, both schools’ governors and STAEG to build something unique and ambitious. We will unite our strengths, histories and values to create an institution of immense educational value, attracting pupils from our local community as well as internationally.
This is a landmark moment for St George’s Ascot.
As we approach our 150th anniversary, creating a through school and welcoming boys from 2027 allows us to build on our strengths while opening an exciting new chapter.
Our partnership with St George’s School Windsor Castle creates a seamless education for 3 to 18 year olds and brings together two proud heritages to deliver something genuinely distinctive, ambitious, values-led and with real impact both locally and internationally.
Hannah Fox, Head of St George’s Ascot
Bringing Windsor and Ascot together creates a genuinely exciting opportunity to build a seamless, high-quality education for girls and boys from early years through to sixth form, while strengthening what already makes both schools so special.
Amber Waite, Principal of STAEG
Find out more about our next chapter

Performing Arts
Find your confidence on stage
Whether taking centre stage in a major musical, performing in a dramatic production, or expressing creativity through dance, our Performing Arts programme gives every pupil the opportunity to discover their talents and grow in confidence.
From Year 7 onwards, pupils can become involved in productions, dance performances and specialist workshops, developing creativity, teamwork and communication skills that will benefit them for life. With professional-standard facilities and expert tuition, there is something for performers of every experience level.
Drama Productions
Drama is one of the most vibrant parts of life at St George's. Throughout the year, pupils have the opportunity to perform in a variety of productions, from Year 7 performances to senior plays and our highly anticipated whole-school musical.
Recent productions have included Oliver!, Beauty and the Beast, Grease, Sister Act and The Sound of Music, involving pupils both on stage and behind the scenes. Those interested in technical theatre can also gain experience in lighting, sound, stage management, set construction, costumes and hair and make-up.
Our productions encourage collaboration, creativity and confidence, while creating unforgettable memories for everyone involved.
Dance
Working in partnership with the Natalie Vinson School of Dance, pupils can enjoy an extensive programme of dance classes suitable for all abilities.
Pupils follow the RAD syllabus (Royal Academy of Dance) and have the opportunity to take Graded and Vocational examinations. Lessons can also be taken as a recreational activity (group and individual lessons). Our students have been extremely successful in their RAD Ballet examinations with 100% gaining a Distinction or Merit. Higher grades (from Grade 6) are awarded UCAS points.
This class is for pupils in Grade 4 Ballet and above. Pupils will improve their strength and flexibility through stretching and Pilates based exercises. Additionally pupils will study pointework or pointework preparation.
Pilates is a popular form of exercise which focuses on the core postural muscles. These help to keep the body balanced and are essential for providing support for the spine. Pilates improves flexibility and teaches awareness of breath control. It requires focus and concentration.
Zumba is a very popular aerobics / dance style combining Latin and International music with a fun and effective workout programme.
Tap has its roots in Harlem, USA and involves the use of the ankles and feet, incorporating different beats and rhythms to music. Not only is tap a very popular form of dance but it's good fun too!
Acro is a form of movement which combines dance with gymnastics. While all dance is physical, Acro is particularly athletic and has unique choreography due to its use of acrobatics in a dance environment. It seamlessly fuses elements of lyrical gymnastics, tricks, balancing, tumbling, ballet and jazz dance.
Dance GCSE
This class is run by the Natalie Vinson School of Dance and Drama off-site in Ascot and can be taken as an extra GCSE in the pupils’ own time.
Natalie Vinson’s GCSE Dance results have been extremely impressive with her pupils achieving 100% pass rates since the course started in 2003 with 95% (100 students) gaining and A*, A or B Grades.

PSHE
Preparing Pupils for Life.
Personal, social, health and economic education helps to equip every pupil to leave St George’s as a capable, confident and connected young people. The programme is underpinned by Spiritual, Moral, Social and Cultural aims and is designed to support the pupils’ wider education and personal development.
The personal, social, health and economics education (PSHE) curriculum is well planned and effective in developing pupils’ understanding of social mattress. [...] Pupils learn that every individual is unique and deserves respect.
ISI Report September 2025
The programme is run for all our Year 7 - Year 11 in timetabled weekly classes. The programme is delivered by specialist teachers in PSHE and also teachers with specific training in relevant areas, such as Information Communication Technology, Science, Religious Studies, Health and Wellbeing and Careers Management. Learning is supported by a series of workshops and lectures delivered by outside agencies, that cover pupil wellbeing and add an important extra dimension to their education.
Our PSHE programme aims to develop each pupil's understanding of themselves, as an individual and in relation to others, helping them to reach their full potential both at school and in their future lives.
The programme explores contemporary issues, the role of the individual in society and nurtures respect for the different nationalities, religions and cultures of others. It is a wonderful journey of self discovery and gives pupils all the skills to reflect on issues, contribute to discussions and understand issues relating to their own protection.
Looking Ahead
PSHE works alongside our Futures programme to help pupils understand themselves, explore their interests and make informed decisions about their future.
From developing confidence and communication skills to exploring careers, financial awareness and the world of work, pupils gradually build the knowledge and independence they need to navigate life beyond St George's.

Making Waves: A Strong Start for St George’s Ascot Performance Swimming Programme
St George’s Ascot is celebrating an exceptional first six months of its Performance Swimming Programme, launched in September 2025.
Beginning with a deliberately selective squad of eight competitive swimmers, the programme is led by Director of Sport Sophie Appleby and Head Performance Coach Nicky Matthews. Early competitive results at the January County Championships have already highlighted the rapid progression of the all-girls team.
Across two championship weekends, the squad achieved:
Five of the eight swimmers have already secured qualifying times for the South East Regional Championships taking place this spring which is a remarkable milestone in the programme’s inaugural year.
57 individual swims
41 lifetime best performances
20 finals appearances
A Fully Integrated Performance Pathway
The Performance Swimming Programme combines high-level training with academic ambition. On-site pool sessions are embedded within the school day, supported by strength and conditioning training, race-skills work and athlete development workshops in sports psychology and nutrition.
Crucially, academic timetables are carefully structured to protect curriculum depth while accommodating training demands. Small class sizes, structured study support and close communication between teachers and coaches ensure that performance development never comes at the expense of academic progress.
The discipline required for high-performance sport translates directly into the classroom. Swimmers learn to manage time, focus under pressure and build resilience. All of which are qualities that support success well beyond the pool.
As a selective squad, each swimmer is known and supported as both an athlete and a learner.
Our aim is not only to develop faster competitive swimmers, but young women who discover the rewards and friendship of being part of a team, alongside the joy of pushing their boundaries and believing in what they can achieve. From there, they carry the focus and ambition learned in the water into every part of their learning, and into the future.
Head Hannah Fox reflects on the programme’s wider ambition.
With scholarships offering fee remission of up to 70% and Swim England club affiliation, the programme provides a distinctive pathway for ambitious female swimmers seeking competitive progression within a nurturing and academically ambitious school environment.
Several Performance Swimming Scholarships have already been awarded for 2026 entry. Applications remain open for 2026 and beyond.

Academic Stretch
Developing curious minds, confident thinkers and a lifelong love of learning.

Futures
From curiosity to confident decisions
Our Futures programme runs throughout the School from Year 7 to Sixth Form, and follows the Gatsby Benchmarks combining academic guidance, personalised support and real-world insight.
Pupils are supported at every stage, from exploring their own strengths and how these might connect with future careers to making informed post-18 decisions about university, degree apprenticeships, employment and more. We believe that success depends not just on what you know, but on how you think, how you adapt, and how well you understand yourself. Through partnerships with organisations such as Unifrog, pupils can engage with a wide range of opportunities that bring potential career pathways to life.
In the early years, the focus is developing personal understanding and curiosity. Through PSHE lessons, co-curricular opportunities, visiting speakers and wider discussion, pupils begin to understand their strengths and interests, build confidence in new areas and explore the world beyond the classroom. This early focus on self-awareness provides the foundation for decision-making for GCSE options and looking further ahead into the future.
As they move into GCSE years, the SGA Futures programme extends further. Pupils are supported to make informed A Level choices, explore possible career pathways and develop a deeper understanding of their skills.
To do this we follow structured guidance and reflection, explore work experience opportunities following GCSEs and take part in external workshops and seminars to support career thinking. It is a time to begin to connect SGA Sixth academic choices with future possibilities.
In Sixth Form, pupils are encouraged to take ownership of their future. They are supported through a structured and highly personalised programme that brings together academic development, reflection and real-world insight. Regular individual meetings with their tutor, the Head of Sixth Form and the Deputy Head, Co-Curricular and Connections, offer opportunities to discuss their post-18 options.
Learning how to learn
All pupils take part in a structured, tailored Executive Function programme, delivered by Mrs Debbie Kratt, Head of Sixth Form. This enables them to manage their time and workload effectively, plan and prioritise, work independently and learn ways to approach challenges with confidence
Academic and super-curricular development
Each Georgian builds depth through completing the Extended Project Qualification (EPQ), subject exploration beyond the classroom and wider reading and research.
Through careers lunches, guest speakers and events, all pupils throughout the school have the opportunity to engage with our alumnae and industry professionals across a wide range of fields. These experiences bring career pathways to life and provide relatable role models. Hearing directly from those who have taken different routes, including university and degree apprenticeships, helps pupils understand that there is no single path to success.
At St George’s, Futures is not just about choosing a destination, it is about developing the skills needed to succeed beyond school. Here they learn to think critically and independently, communicate ideas clearly, manage their time and competing priorities. These skills are embedded across the curriculum, co-curricular programme and Sixth Form experience.

Scholars
Recognising talent. Inspiring curiosity. Developing potential.
At St George’s, our scholars are encouraged to go beyond their strengths and discover what they are capable of. Whether their passion lies in academic study, sport, music, drama, art or performance, our scholarship programmes provide opportunities to develop expertise, challenge themselves and make a meaningful contribution to school life.
Exploring Ideas Beyond the Classroom
St George’s is a community which values scholarship, and pupils can get involved in a number of societies which have an academic focus such as STEM Club, or get involved in activities such as the Model United Nations. Lectures by visiting speakers offer the opportunity to learn more about specific subjects. Senior pupils benefit from an open invitation to attend lectures and seminars organised by Eton College.
Learning Through Discussion
Pupils who are awarded scholarships are invited to a series of lunchtime events with fellow scholars from across the year groups. Over an excellent lunch, the pupils will debate matters of interest with members of staff. We also hold a series of cross-curricular discussions called “In Our Club Time” involving teachers and pupils looking at a variety of topics from the perspective of their own academic subject.
Academic Stretch
Academic scholars are automatically enrolled as members of our lively SGA Stretch group. The group meets regularly to discuss items of intellectual debate, take part in challenges and deliver presentations on matters beyond the curriculum.
Find Out More About Stretch
Co-curricular Scholars Programme
A range of scholarships and exhibitions are awarded for co-curricular activities such as Sport, Drama, Music, and Dance. Pupils who receive these accolades become part of a co-curricular scholars programme which encourages the pupils to analyse their own goals for the academic year ahead and identify targets for their achievement under the guidance of a mentor. There are also visits for scholars to see and analyse professional performers in their fields of interest as well as hearing from speakers discussing issues of importance in lectures.

English as an Additional Language
We have a very strong team in our English as an Additional Language (EAL) department, who work alongside pupils needing support to access the school curriculum.
All our EAL lessons are conducted on a one-to-one basis. Our EAL teachers work closely with academic subject teachers and tutors to ensure that EAL students are receiving the specific language support they need. We also help our students prepare for any external examinations such as IELTS, the English proficiency test accepted by British Universities, and provide the internationally recognised Cambridge exams, should the pupils wish to take this (PET, FCE and CAE), with the final exam taken at a certified test centre. We aim for all the pupils to achieve IELTS 7.5 by the time they leave St George’s ready for university entrance.

pageCache.pageTitle: Music at St George’s | St Georges Ascot
pageCache.text:
Music at St George’s
‘Music for all’ is the guiding principle of the Music Department at St George’s.
Music is embedded in the core curriculum and extends far beyond the classroom, enriching academic study, co-curricular life and wellbeing. Excellence in performance is a defining feature of music at St George’s, and every pupil is encouraged to discover and develop their musical potential.
Choral Tradition and the Chapel Choir
St George’s is particularly renowned for its choral tradition. Our Chapel Choir is of an exceptionally high standard, with membership awarded by audition. Recognisable by their distinctive red cloaks, the choir has sung for members of the Royal Family. They have toured internationally to Salzburg and Vienna and regularly perform at prestigious concerts, weddings and services, including events for the Law Society in London, Eton College, Ascot Racecourse and the Windsor Horse Show. The Chapel Choir has broadcast on BBC Radio 3, recorded three CDs and sings Evensong at various London venues each year.
For many pupils, these experiences open doors to further musical opportunity, including choral scholarships and continued study beyond school. The habits formed here provide a strong foundation for those pursuing music at the highest level.
Music Technology and Recording Suite
St George’s recently opened its new Music Technology Room and Recording Studio, enhancing our already extensive music facilities and technology provision. Designed to support both curriculum and co-curricular learning, the suite provides pupils with access to cutting-edge recording and computer technology, enabling them to explore composition, production and sound engineering. This innovative space supports pupils in developing their creative potential and equips those interested in studio-based careers with valuable, real-world skills and experience.
Performance and Concert Opportunities
Performance opportunities run throughout the year, with termly Junior and Whole School Concerts, seasonal services and celebrations, and the Christmas Carol Service at Windsor Church. In the Spring Term, pupils compete in the House Music Competition, judged by an external adjudicator. The Summer Term features the Jazz and Dance Show with the Jazz Group and Natalie Vinson dancers, and concludes with Music for a Summer Evening, celebrating Upper Sixth pupils, the Jazz Group and the Chapel Choir with the school community, Governors and parents.
Alongside these formal events, our termly Open Mic Nights provide a more informal but equally valuable platform. These evenings encourage pupils to share original compositions, contemporary repertoire and collaborative performances in a supportive atmosphere.
Instrumental and Vocal Tuition
Instrumental and vocal tuition is a key part of music at St George’s, with over half of pupils taking individual lessons with specialist visiting teachers across a wide range of instruments, including singing, piano, guitar, percussion, violin, clarinet, trumpet and saxophone. Pupils regularly sit ABRSM exams, with many progressing to Diploma level, while Musical Theatre students take Thames Valley University exams and percussionists take Trinity College examinations.
